item.title: Here’s the latest.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Lerer

item.title: Why Haley Stevens Can’t Stop Talking About Abdul El-Sayed
item.description: In a frank interview, she described her disappointment and also said she was considering converting to Judaism. Her fiancé had thoughts, too.
item.dc:creator: Reid J. Epstein
item.media:credit: Nic Antaya for The New York Times
item.media:description: Representative Haley Stevens of Michigan endorsed Dr. Abdul El-Sayed after he defeated her in a Democratic Senate primary in August. In recent weeks, though, her tone has shifted.

item.title: Talarico Makes Final Election Pitch to Texans: ‘You Are My Slingshot’
item.description: The Democratic candidate for Senate has led in polls. But because it’s Texas, he remains the underdog.
item.dc:creator: Robert Draper
item.media:description: James Talarico campaigning in Dallas on Thursday. Mr. Talarico’s race against Ken Paxton, the Texas attorney general, may well decide which party controls the Senate.

item.title: Pete Ricketts Leads Dan Osborn in Nebraska Senate Race, Poll Finds
item.description: Voters see Dan Osborn, the independent seeking to unseat Senator Pete Ricketts, as more like a Democrat than an independent, a Times/Siena poll found.
item.dc:creator: Ruth Igielnik and Emily Davies

item.title: Trump and GOP Close Midterms With Ugly Personal Attacks
item.description: Facing backlash over inflation and anger with the president, Republicans have turned to an onslaught of baseless claims about Democratic candidates.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk and Sam Easter
item.media:description: President Trump has repeatedly redrawn the bounds of acceptable discourse in American politics. Many Republicans are following his lead.

item.title: As Midterms Near, Top Law Firms That Capitulated to Trump Are on the Sidelines
item.description: None of the firms that struck deals to avoid crippling executive orders are publicly involved in the major legal efforts to check the Trump administration’s attempts to meddle in the midterm elections, a review by The New York Times shows.
item.dc:creator: Michael S. Schmidt and Jim Rutenberg
item.category: National Assn for the Advancement of Colored People
item.media:description: The lawyer Norm Eisen is preparing to lead a coalition that has vowed to stop President Trump if he tries to interfere in the midterm elections.

item.title: A Halloween Tale: Ghost Stories of the U.S. Capitol
item.description: The ghost stories, dating back to the 19th century, are fitting for a building where the past rarely stays dead.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Diaz and Alex Kent

item.title: How Disabled Children Were Caught Up in Trump’s Homeless Crackdown
item.description: In its push to clear out people who live on the street and are mentally ill, the Trump administration is targeting legal protections that cover a much bigger population.
item.dc:creator: Maia Spoto
item.media:credit: Agnes Lopez for The New York Times
item.media:description: Medically complex children in Florida like Dylan Webb depend on at-home nurses. The Trump administration has stopped defending a court order that governs their care.

item.title: Voters Usually Ignore Corruption as an Issue. It Now Has Their Attention.
item.description: Voters have shrugged off accusations of corruption for years, believing all politicians are corrupt, but thanks to President Trump’s unpopularity and growing wealth, the issue is breaking through.
item.dc:creator: David Ovalle and Emily Cochrane
item.media:credit: Ash Adams for The New York Times
item.media:description: Some recent polls have shown corruption has risen to the top of issues that voters say they care about most.

item.title: Democrats Need Big Margins in Houston. Can This Progressive Deliver?
item.description: Dr. Letitia Plummer has been polling ahead in the race to lead Harris County, where turnout could decide statewide races.
item.dc:creator: J. David Goodman
item.media:credit: Antranik Tavitian for The New York Times
item.media:description: If elected, Dr. Letitia Plummer would be the state’s highest-ranking Muslim woman in office.

item.title: Judge Blocks Expediting Migrant Children’s Asylum Cases, For Now
item.description: Lawyers for the children praised the pause on fast-tracked interviews of unaccompanied minors, calling it a blow against the Trump administration’s “deportation assembly line.”
item.dc:creator: Madeleine Ngo
item.media:description: An unaccompanied five-year-old migrant surrendered to Border Patrol officers last year.

item.title: Justice Dept. Confirms Alaska Inquiry Even as Its Focus Remains Unclear
item.description: Democrats and former officials have accused the department of pursuing a political goal in the guise of a legal one: to publicize a scheme, sordid but not illegal under state law, damaging to Democrats.
item.dc:creator: Anna Griffin and Glenn Thrush
item.media:description: Michael J. Heyman, the U.S. attorney for Alaska, spoke to the media during a news conference Friday in Anchorage.

item.title: Why Running for the U.S. Senate Is a Rich Person’s Game
item.description: Your Senate candidates are probably richer than you.
item.dc:creator: Jess Bidgood
item.media:description: Senator Pete Ricketts of Nebraska is worth more than $100 million.

item.title: Minnesota Declined to Buy a Prison for $75 Million. D.H.S. Paid $495 Million.
item.description: The recent purchase of the prison to hold immigrants is among the acquisitions facing scrutiny in the Trump administration’s mass deportation push.
item.dc:creator: Ernesto Londoño
item.media:description: The Prairie Correctional Facility was purchased by the Department of Homeland Security to serve as an immigrant detention center in Appleton, Minn.

item.title: Alina Habba’s Husband Ignited Drama in Trump’s Circle. Now He’s Under Scrutiny.
item.description: Turhan Mildon, who married Alina Habba this summer, presents himself as a 29-year-old billionaire with ties to global leaders. His story has inconsistencies.
item.dc:creator: Anatoly Kurmanaev, Tyler Pager and Declan Walsh
item.media:description: Turhan Mildon in Kinshasa in 2023.

item.title: Trump’s Plane Flyover Is a Halloween Trick for Startled D.C. Residents
item.description: A White House social media account said the surprise Air Force One flight was part of a Halloween event hosted by the president and the first lady.
item.dc:creator: Michael Crowley
item.media:description: President Trump and Melania Trump, the first lady, during a Halloween event at the White House on Thursday.

item.title: Appeals Court Again Rejects Trump Effort to Impound California Ballots
item.description: In a 2-to-1 vote, an appeals court panel declined to order the state to set aside more than 20,000 mail-in ballots, calling the notion plainly unconstitutional.
item.dc:creator: Zach Montague
item.media:credit: Mike Kai Chen for The New York Times
item.media:description: Election workers verified the delivery of mail-in ballots collected by police officers from ballot drop boxes in California in August.

item.title: A Resurgent Justice Democrats Could Reshape a Democratic Congress
item.description: Justice Democrats, which gained prominence backing Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, is on track to see more of its candidates elected. Will the party listen to them?
item.dc:creator: Catie Edmondson
item.media:credit: Chet Strange for The New York Times

item.title: Prosecutors Suggest They May Seek Additional Comey Charges
item.description: At a hearing in federal court, prosecutors defended an unusual, 11th-hour criminal case accusing the former F.B.I. director of leaking classified information a decade ago.
item.dc:creator: Devlin Barrett
item.media:credit: Monica Jorge for The New York Times
item.media:description: During President Trump’s second term, the Justice Department has pursued James B. Comey without pause.

item.title: Judge Appoints Special Master to Determine if Trump Officials Lied in Golf Course Suit
item.description: Judge Ana C. Reyes said an outside investigator would help determine whether parks officials or Justice Department lawyers withheld plans for Washington’s East Potomac Park.
item.dc:creator: Zach Montague
item.media:description: A federal judge on Friday called for an investigation into whether the Trump administration concealed its plans to renovate a public golf course at East Potomac Park.

item.title: Distaste for Lavrov Forces U.S. to Cancel G20 Photo Session in Atlanta
item.description: Some European foreign ministers had refused to pose alongside Russia’s top diplomat, Sergey Lavrov, at a Group of 20 gathering hosted by the United States.
item.dc:creator: Michael Crowley
item.media:credit: Erik S. Lesser/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: Many European diplomats believe that Russian officials like Sergey Lavrov should be shunned over Moscow’s war in Ukraine.

item.title: El-Sayed Clashes With Former Primary Rival Who Demanded His Apology
item.description: Dr. Abdul El-Sayed and Representative Haley Stevens traded sharply critical comments Friday, escalating intraparty tensions in Michigan’s pivotal Senate race.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk
item.media:credit: Nic Antaya for The New York Times
item.media:description: Representative Haley Stevens of Michigan has agreed to campaign with her former Senate primary opponent Dr. Abdul El-Sayed.

item.title: Steve Hilton Tries Anything as a G.O.P. Long Shot in California
item.description: Steve Hilton is attempting to become governor in a state that hasn’t elected a Republican to the top job in 20 years.
item.dc:creator: Laurel Rosenhall
item.media:credit: Philip Cheung for The New York Times
item.media:description: Offering $3-a-gallon gas was both a way for Mr. Hilton to attract voters and a manifestation of one of his many policy proposals.

item.title: Democrats, Hopeful All Over the Senate Map, Remain Jittery About Iowa
item.description: In the final days of the race, Josh Turek, the Democratic Senate nominee, appears to be in a dead heat against his Republican rival, Representative Ashley Hinson.
item.dc:creator: Bayliss Wagner
item.media:credit: KC McGinnis for The New York Times
item.media:description: Josh Turek, the Democratic nominee for Senate in Iowa, is a state representative and former Paralympian who has spent much of this year introducing himself to the state’s voters.

item.title: Pope Leo Votes by Mail, From the Vatican, in Illinois Midterm Election
item.description: Pope Leo may be the first pope to vote in a national election, Vatican experts said.
item.dc:creator: Julie Bosman and Elisabetta Povoledo
item.media:description: Pope Leo XIV requested a mail-in ballot for the midterm elections from his home state of Illinois.

item.title: Houston Grand Jury Indicts ICE Agent on Charges of Ramming Man in Chase
item.description: The agent is facing charges of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon. The immigrant who was struck is recovering from severe leg injuries.
item.dc:creator: Edgar Sandoval

item.title: Former Patient Files Class-Action Lawsuit Against Senator Marshall
item.description: The Republican sued more than 700 patients during his former career as a physician. The suit accuses him of charging illegally high interest rates.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Kliff
item.media:description: Senator Roger Marshall is involved in a lawsuit regarding high interest rates he charged patients on outstanding bills.

item.title: Trump Adds Midterm Rallies in Kansas and Iowa After Initially Canceling Events
item.description: The back-and-forth over President Trump’s schedule comes as polls show Republicans are in danger of losing seats, including in areas he won handily in 2024.
item.dc:creator: Tyler Pager

item.title: Judge Bars Trump Administration From Threatening to Prosecute Election Workers in California
item.description: The ruling could deprive the Justice Department of its most important leverage in extracting concessions from local officials, the threat of prosecution.
item.dc:creator: Glenn Thrush
item.media:description: An election worker sorting ballot envelopes at the Orange County Registrar of Voters in Santa Ana, Calif., on Wednesday.

item.title: Democrats and Republicans Share Dueling Health Care Messages in Final Midterms Push
item.description: After concentrating on the high price of gas and groceries, Democrats are using health costs to make their case about an “affordability crisis.”
item.dc:creator: Sheryl Gay Stolberg
item.category: Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (2010)
item.media:credit: Jenn Ackerman for The New York Times
item.media:description: “People are really, really hanging on by a thread here,” said Rebecca Cooke, a Democratic congressional candidate in Wisconsin who has made health care costs a central issue of her campaign.

item.title: Pelosi Splits With Mamdani and El-Sayed on Israel
item.description: In a podcast interview, she asserted that criticism of Israel from some prominent Democrats did not reflect the views of the party itself.
item.dc:creator: John Yoon
item.media:credit: Mike Kai Chen for The New York Times
item.media:description: Nancy Pelosi criticized Mayor Zohran Mamdani of New York and Dr. Abdul El-Sayed over their refusal to endorse Israel as a Jewish state.

item.title: Elon Musk Predicts End of Democracy if Midterm Elections Favor Democrats
item.description: Mr. Musk’s rhetoric, heated as it is, partly explains why he has spent nearly $475 million to back Republicans in the midterms.
item.dc:creator: Theodore Schleifer
item.media:credit: Brendan McDermid/Reuters; Demetrius Freeman for The New York Times

item.title: The Justice Department’s Unusual Election-Year Activity
item.description: Federal prosecutors have targeted President Trump’s political opponents and sued states over election administration just before the midterms. Devlin Barrett, a reporter for The New York Times, explains how this activity is compared with the Justice Department’s usual election-year behavior.
item.dc:creator: Devlin Barrett, Paul Abowd, Nikolay Nikolov, Rafaela Balster, Whitney Shefte, Nour Idriss and Laura Salaberry
